        O’Neal never really got a good answer as to what his problem really is and didn’t even get any good advice on how to improve. Fortunately for us, there will never be a dull moment with O’Neal at our side.
story.STORY_FLEET_142:
Darrien is the legendary creator of the mysterious Darkblood base. This base has technological equipment that is even better than the Empire’s Laboratory, along with some mad scientists. This is the birthplace of state of the art technology. They even make some secret weapons for the Empire that receive interstellar restrictions.
        According to the Empire’s secret records, Darrien is an illegitimate child of the family, but he is also a genius researcher and commander. Maybe just a hair away from the line between genius and insane. When the four Empires of the galaxy fell into war, Darrien was 16. At such a young age, he was still able to develop a terribly destructive weapon. After winning three large-scale battles, he had to go on trial at the Interstellar Court.
        His father tearfully ensured the court that he would keep Darrien within the house and restrict his research. Darrien, though, just laughed at everyone present in the courtroom. He thought that they were an uncivilized bunch, incapable of understanding the wonders of science. It was because they were ignorant that they were afraid. 
        Darrien’s contemptuousness resulted in a 3300 year prison sentence. As the judge passed down the verdict he said, “since people of this time cannot understand your technology, maybe the peoples of 3300 years in the future can appreciate what you’ve made.” 
        After two years, Darrien refused to just waste away in prison, and he made an agreement with the first emperor. He would be forever faithful in exchange for a chance at secret escape. Really, he just wanted to prove himself to his father. 
        Darren became a founding father of the Galactic Empire. He declined the Emperor, though, and took his children far away, becoming a kind of secret nobleman. Since his father had already passed away, his glory and accomplishments meant nothing to him. He now only respected the promise he made when leaving jail, to serve the empire forever.
        The man on this base could be the progeny of that genius of 400 years ago, or it could really be the same Darrien of legend, able to use the miracles of science to prolong his life. Regardless, it was Darrien who appeared at the opportune moment of the battle between humankind and Shadow Will and brought with him brand new Galactonite and power, becoming one of the most important factors of the human’s victory.
        There is no need to fear the unknown out in the universe. The bounds of science are endless.
story.STORY_FLEET_158:
What is do Justice and Evil really mean? 

Many people have considered this question, but no one seems to have found an answer. Some people say that destroying a city for the sake of a single person is evil. Others say that fighting for one’s country and people is righteous. In ancient times, monks would only eat plants in order not to harm any living being. Now after we have found a planet dominated by plants, we are forced to admit: regardless of the motive behind a killing, it is difficult to judge it as just or evil. 
        Gambit is the archbishop and leader of the Divine Federation. He dedicates his life to the light and to justice, but he is slipping into the darkness. 
        He has all the memories and abilities of Gambit, but he isn’t that person. “Gambit” knows the history of his personage. His DNA and early memories come from the Imperial Fleet, but he knows he is but a clone created by Shadow Will.
        When the Apostles hit a wall in their gene mutation experiments, the next project was simple: clones and implications. 
        After no longer desiring to be the creator and controller of all and using Shadow Will’s technology, everything would go more smoothly. Dark Gambit could control his own thoughts and body, but he can’t resist the consciousness implanted by Shadow Will. He clearly recognizes what his other half is fighting for, but he could easily destroy all the human ships he had sworn to protect forever. 
        Consciousness is truly amazing, Dark Gambit though. Regardless of how devout he used to be, it couldn’t stop him from sinking into the darkness. The moment he walked out of the lab, the past and the present had already stitched themselves together seamlessly. Just like a two-sided coin, if the two sides are forced apart, its existence is no longer complete. 
        Then what is justice, and what is evil? Dark Gambit doesn’t have an answer to this question. His answer were the embers of the stars.
story.STORY_FLEET_167:
For most people, the word “war” is generally a heavy, cruel one. It is a defiance of morals and life. Smoke clouds, blazes of fire, particle cannons: no one associates these things with beauty. Valerie, on the other hand, feels the life breath of music in war. 
        The ever expanding frontier of the Empire gradually increase the Galaxy Empire’s burden. Even the fastest waves cannot spread the imperial edicts quickly enough to every corner of the empire. And of course for those living on the other side of the galaxy, these messages are not very interesting. No farmers care whether the Emperor visited the Nami planet or not, or if some rich person goes broke due to careless spending. People only care about what is around them, and the trifling details of their lives have already stifled their dreams. 
        Valerie, though, stridently holds on to her dreams. She loves music, and Opal is her idol. As a child, Valerie loved leafing through the comics sent out by the Empire to all its colonies. The holographic images of the Imperial Conservatory captured the heart of this little girl. From then on, studying and living in the places described in those comics was her most heartfelt wish. She taught herself basic music theory and the imperial dialect. She even convinced her parents to financially support her trip. Finally, Valerie arrived at the heart of the Empire with her childhood sweetheart. Surprisingly, the music conservatory from the comics had been changed into a military academy! 
        Since study was the purpose of her journey, she reluctantly entered the Military Academy. Fortunately, she discovered that battle could be even more exciting than music. She often compared battle to music. The Protectors have the strongest music, while Strikers and Rangers are the passionate rhythm. Rovers are the fading and free vibrato, and Destroyers are the crescendo and climax of the song. And the commanders control the tempo and integration of different ships and tactics. It’s just like a conductor controlling a performance!
        After Valerie stepped onto the battlefield, she quickly became a legend of the generation with her unique battle techniques. If battle is a song, let’s play together with her the Symphony of Victory!
story.STORY_FLEET_164:
“Hey, up and at ‘em! You youngsters should be brimming with energy!”
        Jackie, the engineering instructor, is known as the ghost engineer and is a passionate man. Every day of training, he shouts the new recruits awake and kicks their beds.
        “Guess what! Some people say that the reason Jackie is always wearing goggles and a gas mask is that he has tiny mouse eyes and a mouthful of sharp teeth!”
        “Huh? Isn’t this the coolest style right now? Don’t compare me with some filthy little creature,” Jackie thought when he overheard these rumors. 
        “You know what? The reason Jackie makes such a ruckus every morning is because he is actually 300 years old, and yelling like that makes him feel younger!”
        “What?? I’m in the prime of my youth at not even 30 years old yet!” Jackie though when he heard some other new recruits talking about him.
        “I’ll tell ya’ what. The reason Jackie is called the Ghost Engineer is because people who rode in the ship he modified would run into the ghosts people talk about from legends.”
        “Those hooligans! My name comes from the fact that I could modify ships so well that it scared the others as if they had seen a ghost! Nothing about real ghosts!” Jackie complained when he heard even more kids talking about him.
        To help his reputation, during Valentine’s Day, Jackie took all the new recruits to a holiday resort - Palm Planet. He hoped that showing up in his bathing suit with a hand around his girlfriend would be enough to stamp out all the rumors. It ended up that even more rumors began circulating...
        Jackie, Jackie...
Since he is able to hear microwaves and human brainwaves, although his reputation was tarnished by the new recruits, he still was one of the mentors they remembered most after graduating. The newbies generally come in scared of battle or feeling uncomfortable in their new environment. Only someone who could understand how they felt and join their circle could produce the best training plans, and Jackie was able to do that. He was able to cultivate better and better soldiers for the Imperial Fleet.
        “Hey, look alive, boys! Time to start the day!” 
Jackie’s bellowing voice awoke the recruits for another day and got them ready for battle. Good luck!
story.STORY_FLEET_163:
Natalie does not fear death. She believes that humans can achieve final victory against Shadow Will because, although mankind has the desire to survive, they also are willing to sacrifice themselves for their brethren if need be. 
        When Shadow Will was pushed back to the edge of a black hole by the galactic alliance, according to reports from the fourth fleet, the Apolstles’ fleet had already lost 74.59% power. Imperial specialists analyzed that, at the current downward spiral of Shadow Will, victory for the Empire was imminent. With victory within their grasp, the emperor had already planned out the victory processions. Unexpectedly, the tides of battle turned, and just as the humans let up a bit, Shadow Will executed its final plan to drag the humans to death together with them.
        Shadow Will is using the bowl-shaped force field created by the pale star to pull the ships of both sides in the direction of the black star behind Shadow Will! If they don’t break the force field in time and are unable to get out of the black star’s gravisphere, all Imperial ships will be destroyed. 
        Natalie and her crew are the Heaven Cleft Movement’s most direct forces. Their mission is to assist the legendary commander Darren by breaking through Shadow Will’s final Special Forces, enter the peculiar forcefield created by countless pale stars, and find the focal point of the forcefield within the electronic turbulence. By just destroying those few pale stars and destroying the equilibrium of the forcefield, the entire field will be no more. Shadow Will is unable to remove itself from the gravisphere of the black hole, so by just destroying the forcefield, humanity will claim victory and live to fight on.
        “If we make it back alive, we’ll become the heroes of humankind.” Though the chance of survival is slim, but as long as the fighting spirit is kept alive, we can create a new future out of this seeming impossibility.
story.STORY_FLEET_213:
On April Fool’s Day morning, Duomilian received his transfer to the Lawsry district. Upon seeing this news, the young man of nobility dropped and shattered his cup of black tea, and the butler Remy cleaned the ceramic shards up for him. Duomilian opened wide the deep purple curtains of his window and sunlight came cascading into every corner of the room. 
        The remote Lawsry district was not a strategic stronghold and has never even reported an invasion alert higher than level 2. Perhaps those who detest war or wish to retire would enjoy going to a peaceful region, but the ambitious Duomilian certainly doesn’t want to go.
        It is a soldier’s nature to obey, and Remy had already begun preparing the necessities for Duomilian’s long journey. What if all of his long waiting produced just this tiny sliver of hope? He started questioning whether he had made the right decisions. Instructions, rules, maturity... Under the restraints, there were still some things that kept beating inside him. 
        The Lawsry district is the closest one from the Triffid Nebula battlefield. After that battle, the Empire has been peaceful for the past 3 months. But maybe a little too peacful. Duomilian’s intuition told him that the end of a battle isn’t necessarily the end of the story. 
        “Then I’ll accept the mission and go to the Lawsry District. Maybe it’s the fresh start I need,” he said.
story.STORY_FLEET_141:
Planet Paradise is a world of eternal day and eternal night. The rigid orbit and rotation of this planet divides it into two sides: one of never ending daylight and the other of permanent ice fields. 
        More than 80% of the residents on this planet live in the daylight zone. The inexhaustible solar energy and sophisticated scientific applications endow the residents here with a rich life. They stick rigidly to the Empire’s standard rest time. Each person is proud to be a cog in this social wheel where everyone every day works meticulously for 10 hours, plays for 6 hours, and spends the rest of the time sleeping. There is no darkness and no crime in the daylight zone. Everyone who dares speak out or question is banished to the night zone by the Paradise Governor. Everyone thinks that those evil-doers banished to the night zone will simply become gravestones on the frigid plains, but they underestimate humans’ survival instincts. 
        Red City is the largest in the night zone. Cabal distributes food to all the households and then spreads his dark wings to be caught in the powerful gales of the ice planes. The winds here are actually not as strong as those in the daylight zone, but the gravity is only 75% that of the daytime zone’s. This allows well-trained soldiers to remain airborne a considerable amount of time with their wind wings. However, limited resources have made wind wings a privilege for a minority of lucky few. Cabal is one of a nameless order of guardians protecting Red City. (The night zone may be known as a concentration camp for criminals, but their offspring and other innocent people live here too). Protecting the defenseless citizens is Cabal’s creed. The night zone took away people’s ability to sense light in their eyes so sin, grudge, and despair are always brewing inside them... But the darker this place is, the more it needs some fearless people to take a stand and protect the bottom rung of humanity from chaos. 
        Planet Paradise’s new Governor refuses to allow the night zone to be a criminal’s playground. He therefore has implored the Empire to dispatch a fleet to completely annihilate that other side of Planet Paradise. Cabal, most powerful of that dark order, has no choice but to rise up. He must prevent this plan for annihilation and use this opportunity to prove to the Empire that the Governor’s long standing policy to exile all the criminals and dissidents is fundamentally wrong. There doubtless are impenitent sinners, but humans are always capable of learning from their mistakes. There are no perfect societies, so you can’t just silence all questioning voices. If humans can do nothing more than complete their appointed tasks, then they have lost their powers of creation and vitality.
        The Empire is unable to deny Planet Paradise because they have a steadily growing economy and their reports they send every year are impeccable. At the same time, the Empire cannot overlook Cabal. For a hundred years, Planet Paradise has produced very few people of note, and there have been no breakthroughs in the fields of art or science.
        The plan to destroy the night zone was put on hold, and Cabal joined the Imperial Fleet to try and defend the innocent lives of night zone. He will be a spokesman for the night zone, and he will fight to give them a future.
story.STORY_FLEET_166:
Receive orders.
Engage enemy.
Clinch victory.
        This is the extent of Boris’ existence.
        Boris was one of the first bio-soldiers when humans set out to explore outer space. In order to win battles, some soldiers were willing to undergo mecha modifications and swap out their skeletons and important organs for metals ones. They sacrificed their human identity for more power. After the passing of many years, the only vestige of this batch of bio-soldiers is Boris. 
        Sonia once told Boris that, with the Empire’s current level of technology, they would be able to swap out all the cold mechanical bones in his body and give him back a totally human body, a human identity. Boris had forgotten what it was like to live a normal human life, though. Family, friends, even his fellow soldiers that underwent the same mechanical modifications; they were all long gone. Battle and victory became the only things Boris believed in.
        Later on, while exploring the Elemental Dimension, the Imperial Fleet discovered a batch of brand new materials which could be used to enhance bio-soldiers. After this second round of modifications, Boris became even stronger than before. Most strangely of all, some of the materials from his earlier modifications resonated with the new materials from the Elemental Dimension. It is estimated now that Boris has surpassed the highest level ever thought possible for mecha soldiers. 
        This newfound power made Boris release tremor of what sounded like laughter from his alloy chest. This venerated soldier will remain in the Empire and stick to the faith he has always maintained.
Receive orders.
Engage enemy.
Clinch Victory.
story.STORY_FLEET_170:
Prophecies, my friend, are not black magic, nor the workings of witches and necromancers. Nor are they the emperor’s words. We are talking about Aquos, a Vaterian with the power of real prophecy.
        In the eyes of the people, Aquos is the incarnation of the deep blue ocean, seemingly able to answer all questions put to him. He can help people make the wisest decision. He is miraculously able to foresee the changes of every battle and provide the most useful strategy. It is with this power that he earned his respect.
        It was not until Aquos met a never before seen race, the humans, that he struggled to find the right course of action. This Vaterian prophet frankly stated that he could not provide any useful strategy to take. It was at this point that Aquos’ battle companions realized that his prophetic abilities were not really miracles, but just an uncanny ability to scan reports for the most useful information and perform exquisite analysis. 
        With enough information, Aquos was nearly able to predict the exact future before it happened. The more information he gets ahold of, the more accurate his predictions. Any possibility of the future is based on happenings of the past or the present. If a storm was kicked up by a butterfly 3km away, then you just need to have information on this butterfly to determine the effect its wings have on the atmosphere, and you can completely predict the beginning of another storm 3km away. 
        After people and Aquos became allies, he became the first Vaterian in the human fleet. This mysterious prophet has an unquenchable thirst for information, so the data which humans gather is of vital importance to him. It’s all for the next miraculous prophecy.
story.STORY_FLEET_156:
The universe is a grand symphony. No one was around no hear the first note played 10^e-43 seconds ago, but it is possible calculate when it will end. We are unable to remember the time in our childhood when our consciousness became gradually more clear, but technology is already able to predict lifespan.
        Dark Ar’turis can clearly remember when his neural system came to be. The connected consciousness of the Apostles allows him to clearly feel the exact moment when he could feel. That which follows the transmission of weak bio-electricity is not the elation of life, but a clarity of path.
        Battle is a warrior’s only command, but what if a warriors awakens after the battle is over? Ar’turis fled from a lab 5000m below the surface of the planet. The artificial surface of the Hefa base had already crumbled to ruins and heavy ion cannons melted nearly every other building. Due to the importance of the Hefa base, the Empire has dispatched two fleets of soldier groups to clean up the debris. With their life detection devices, the soldiers discovered Dark Ar’turis standing under the remains, watching the slow sinking of the twin blue stars. Subsequently, all 33,000 soldiers of the mission were killed.
        Upon learning this news, the Empire assembled a special force to investigate. However, no fleet can approach the Hefa base safely. Aimless in his life, Dark Ar’turis now sees all life forms which dare enter there range of his radar as enemies. The underground lab on the Hefa base once was one of the three main Dark Shadow labs. Dark Ar’turis initiated the emergency protocol, discarded the artificial crest of the asteroid, and turned this lab into a temporary fortress. According to the Empire, if he doesn’t give up, this small fortress could resist for up to three years. As the first large scale battle on the Elemental Dimension is about to start, the Empire doesn’t want to give up Dark Ar’turis, and they certainly don’t want to waste troops on this tiny fortress. 
        The Empire has implored Arturis himself to convince Dark Ar’turis, but he denied. His body and the clone’s are mirror images, so he understands completely why Dark Ar’turis would want to fight to his last breath. 
        A few days later, however, Dark Ar’turis appeared on the battlefield of the Water Demon planet battle on the side of the humans. Many commanders speculated on the reasons why Dark Ar’turis would come to the aid of the humans, but with such a powerful ally they must certainly win the battle of the Water Demon planet!
story.STORY_FLEET_165:
How long can a person hold out in a hopeless situation? Hartman just may be the one who can give you the answer. Months ago, this hero was an exile on the Ossway Star, known as the tomb of criminals. Most criminals of the Empire are more willing to rot to death in prison than to be exiled that hopeless place.
        Countless Imperial Defenders crowd together in the sky, and on the ground is a dry rocky surface with rich Galactonite Veins. Exiled criminals use mined Galactonite ore to exchange for food and water. Of course, if you are willing, you don’t have to bend the knee to the Empire. A giant breed of Death Worms live natively on this planet. Armed with only the most crude mining tolls, some convicts hunt these worms, but usually forfeit their lives as the price. In this grave for convicts, reputation and honor mean far less than a bottle of life replenishing water. 
        On Ossway, your former identity and name are replaced entirely by a number on the side of your head. Innocent or not, extreme vigilance and strictly enforced supply control causes all to lose hope. Hartmann, however, is an exception. Claiming to be the commander of a legion of holy knights, he has been scheming to escape since his arrival. The young should not have to rot in an early tomb, he thinks. Hartmann clearly knows that he is not a “Traitor of Humanity,” but only after leaving this place can he use his evidence to clear his name.
        Storing up food and other supplies, using limited resources to fit crudely made ships, researching the Defender Ship’s patterns, he prepared everything. Though escaping from Ossway is a serious crime, it is nothing when compared to the besmirched pride of a knight. Everything was going according to plan, but all the difficulties were reminding Hartmann how hard it would be to escape. The trials and tribulations he faced took a toll on his spirits, and he knew giving up would be sweet release, but Hartmann yearned for freedom among the stars. 
        After the Dusk Wars broke out, the Empire needed more and more troops and supplies. This was the chance that Hartmann had been waiting for. 
        Apart from evidence, the best way to clear his name of “Traitor of Humanity” would be to kill as many aliens as he could. Hartmann successfully made it off Ossway and appeared on the battlefield. To everyone's surprise, he saved an entire fleet, proving that he hadn’t just been muddling through his days in the “Criminal’s Tomb.” After ten years in exile, this hero returned to the battlefield and won a war for humankind in brilliant fashion. 
        We extend our thanks to Hartmann! Fortunately, we didn’t lose this hero to human carelessness!
story.STORY_FLEET_172:
When different races and civilizations meet, what is most likely to happen? War, of course. Every organism that can change and manipulate nature on a large scale will face the problem between development speed and resource collecting. 
        Mennonites are a race with bodies composed over 80% of inorganic matter. This peculiar evolutionary trait was initially began in order to avoid resource battles with organic beings. But the unequal distribution of resources in the Elemental Plain and threats from other universes made avoiding war impossible for organisms living there. The evolutionary traits that originally had them live in harmony eventually turned to traits with more destructive power. 
        According to authority, inorganic life forms adapt better to cruel environments than organic beings. They have a stable structure which gives them the capability of enduring over organic beings. They can even be exposed to radiation for a period of time. Mennonites are some of the most powerful soldiers in the Elemental Dimension, but this doesn’t mean they can rule the universe.
        Mennonites and the so-called “Star Burners” of the Sara Mande District have harbored grudges for one another over thousands of years. Neither the learned Sylph people nor the Vaterians gifted in intelligence collection understand the history of the wars between the Mennonites and Star Burners. In the Menno District, every newly born life form bears the burden of battle. They are told that the Star Burners are vulgar and base, and the Mennonites have the duty to exterminate them from the universe. Growing up hearing these kinds of messages, the new Mennonite soldiers carry a strong sense of responsibility after reaching maturity. This may explain why the wars have lasted for thousands of years. 
        “Star Burners? Don’t believe those guys. Please allow me to express a most sincere welcome on behalf of the Mennonites to you, friend.” From the “Galaxy Legend Interstellar Report,” reported from the Universe Exploration Force’s first visit with Menno Ambassador Aethos.
story.STORY_FLEET_176:
Lily
        Lily became one of the most well-known Commanders on the very first day she arrived at the Imperial Fleet. This was due only in part to her power. Even more important was her love for good food!
        The fact that she is able to eat uninterrupted for several hours at the welcome banquet left the Commanders with a new found respect for her, but it is nothing to do with her having an oversized stomach. Rather it is because on Lily's planet, the enzymes in their bodies are several hundred times more active than in those of the Empire. If they so wish they are able to consume their body weight in food in a short space of time.
        Six years ago, the 11 year old Lily received a letter of admission to the Mathematics Department at University. She encountered an attack by the Primus Legion during a vacation she took before finishing her coursework. The super battleship built by the Apostles was being controlled by enemies of the Empire, and they stole technology from the battleship to build more drones. This attack was totally unforeseen by the Empire’s defending troops. When the fleet engaged in battle with one of the Primus ships saw the Primus Legion blocking out the sun, they panicked. In their panic, they let the Primus Legion break through the front lines and hundreds of planets incurred the wrath of the Primus Legion. One of those planets was the one Lily was going to for vacation.
        Buried under layers of rubble, she waited in the darkness for the Reaper to take her away. Unable to keep track of time, she kept alert by humming tunes to herself. When the Imperial Fleet rescued her from the wreckage and she tasted fresh air once again, she immediately decided to join their team. Their uniforms had already left an indelible mark in her mind.
        Of course, Lily would later wear the uniform as she had wanted to after graduating from the Military Academy with flying colors.
story.STORY_FLEET_178:
Mystery surrounds the birth of Lazarus. The first time she talked about her past, if you weren’t there to see her for yourself, you’d think her story was the product of an unpublished other-dimension short story by a second rate author. 
        The universe has given birth to all kinds of races. They may have advanced technology, strong bodies, or surprising reproductive abilities, but all races must face challenges from the natural world and from other races. There may be visitors from a parallel dimension that break through time and space and arrive for survival or for exploration. They may not even have a clear motive.
        Lazarus is a creation from a civilization of an unknown galaxy. According to the information saved in her brain, those visitors with “unimaginable” technology that came to the fringes of the Elemental Dimension passed through millions of light years to get to the Green Algae Planet. They collected the electromagnetic radiation and energy spectrums being spread nonstop to the surrounding regions by that planet. The coding became Lazarus’ consciousness. They then used a material from another space and time with a material from the Elemental Dimension to create Lazarus’ outer form. After completion, they left the Elemental Dimension and headed back to their own galaxy. No one knows why they did what they did. Lazarus was simply left behind, lying in sleep deep with the Green Algae Planet’s crust, waiting for the next visitors. 
        “And that is my story.” Lazarus finished. That is the past she remembered. Human commanders in the fleet find it very hard to believe her story, except Vitos, who also comes from Sylph District.
story.STORY_FLEET_169:
The Holy land of Green Algae is but a shimmering speck of green in the sky to Vitos. Playing the Vitospipes and enjoying the sounds of different shaped leaves blowing in the wind, Vitos wished he could be like those ancient, silent trees, let his spirit be free, and return to the land of his ancestors: Green Algae. 
        Regardless of which version of Sylphian legend to which you ascribe, Green Algae is always named as the first life form in the galaxy. When this planet-sized organism floated through the galaxy for countless years, it felt the desolation and loneliness of the surrounding areas. Green Algae decided to split itself into millions of spores. After sacrificing its soul, Green Algae relinquished its self-awareness and stopped in the Sylph district. Those millions of spores that descended into the surrounding planets were the earliest ancestors of Vitos and the Sylphians. 
        Whether or not you believe the tale, Vitos believes that these ancient stories reveal at least some part of the truth. Even if Green Algae isn’t the real birthplace of the Sylphians, they all can still feel its call. This feeling is not just belief. It’s like a bird yearning for its home. 
        However, before the human fleet came to the Sylph district, not a single Sylphian could successfully make it back to Green Algae. There certainly were Sylphians who only yearned for tranquility, worshipped their holy land, or lacked progressive spirit, but the electromagnetic radiation in the Green Algae surroundings was truly their fatal blow. Sylphians who died a natural death or suffered an accident could use part of their body’s to renew growth, and within a certain period of time, rejuvenate themselves like new. But the electromagnetic radiation from the Green Algae Planet completely destroyed the Sylphian people’s cellular composition, rendering them unable to regenerate. 
        Vitos had already caught word of the humans who had come from another region. His war-mongering “neighbors” were stopped by the electromagnetic radiation. According to war reports from The Water Demon and Dusk, the race from beyond the stars could control the electromagnetism to create a murderous weapon. Maybe they would fulfill the prophecy. New friends “from beyond the stars who pass through the blighted depths will begin the Third Age of Civilization from the Holy Land.”
story.STORY_FLEET_159:
After 791 days away, Celeste entered again into the City of Furious Wind airspace. The giant space fortress was just like the one of her memories. However, from the look of those patrol ships and defense satellites three times the size as before, it looks like this space fortress wasn’t exactly the City of Furious Wind from two years before.        
        After Katiya Storm left the City of Furious Wind, the Vengeance Party controlled two thirds of the senators of the City. From the Galaxy Empire’s view, the City of Furious Wind’s history was far from perfect. After the Barnard Empire was overthrown, the descendants were unwilling to bend knee to the Galaxy Empire, so they went to the Andromeda system and established Vengeance City. During the three hundred years after its founding, many people who broke off from the Galaxy Empire joined them. Three hundred years is more than enough time to forget their hate, though. Like her grandfather, Katiya who left the Empire after suffering an attack and came here. But now back in the Imperial Fleet, the people of the City of Furious Wind will also think back on their home.
        Her former lover, Folin was the grandson of the Vengeance Party’s ringleader: Shio. When Celeste asked for permission to land and the command tower’s control center respectfully asked her to use the guest landing pad G32, she knew everything had changed. Celeste’s faction had been eroded away by Shio. She didn’t know what had become of the special landing pad Folin had specially built for her. She left the City of Furious Wind so that her grandfather would let her be with Folin, but her 791 days of waiting were proof that what she dreaded most had come true. 
        “Harnessing the power to control Primus’ core is enough to rejuvenate the past glory of our ancestors!” Celeste didn’t land on landing platform G32 as instructed. For reasons unknown, she suspected that the voice speaking to her through the City of Furious Wind’s secret channel was Folin’s, but it wasn’t as sweet as before.
        Love isn’t all there is to life, Dark Celeste. The most important thing now is to bid farewell to the City of Furious Wind and get the information back to the Galaxy Empire.
story.STORY_FLEET_182:
The most ancient and powerful of her kind, the Shamen Queen commanded the armies of the Sara Mande District. The art of warfare and came to her as easily as breathing, and within her chest beat the heart of a champion. Her enemies fell before her forces, and she counted the fear in her enemy's eyes as a badge of honor. 

After a time, once every last corner of Elemental Dimension fell under the Shamen Queen's rule, fighting ceased and the armies of Sara Mande District relaxed. Instead of peace and prosperity - which was the hope of Shamen Queen - she gazed about her and saw how deteriorated and rusted the ships had become, and how lazy and complacent her armies and people had become. Instead of seizing the peace they had won, and working toward a brighter future, the people sought solitary fame and fortune and had forgotten how to avoid heavy artillery and meteorites. The Shamen Queen, feeling the full weight of the blame for the decline of all that she had built up, gave up her rights of title and territories, left Elemental Dimension and traveled in solitude among the districts. She believed there must be a solution out among her people.

The Shamen Queen searched far and wide, moving from district to district seeking an unknown new hope for her people of Sara Mande. After a time, numerous soldiers began to follow her, urging her to reclaim her throne and lead them again. The Shamen Queen refused, stating that although she carried great power within her, it alone was not enough to make her the great ruler she wanted for her people. 

And so her search continued...

Until the day strange new creatures broke through the barriers of space and entered the Elemental Dimension. War came swiftly and enveloped the Elemental Dimension. The Shamen Queen's heart leapt. Finally! Blood surged through her veins, invigorating her, spurring her into action. She suppressed part of her power and disguised herself as one of the creatures - "humans", they called themselves. Able to fit in as one of the humans, she joined the Elemental Dimension reinforcements fleet on the side of the Empire at the battle of Metal Heart. 

during her time fighting alongside these new creatures, she found them to be curious and far more interesting she imagined they would be. Though she currently fought on the side of the Empire, she imagined a future in which the armies of Sara Mande, restored to their former glory, would one day conquer these humans and rule their Galaxy.

She had lived for so long that every unexpected moment seemed beautiful to her. She could feel it deep in her bones: these would be grand and glorious times.
story.STORY_FLEET_168:
Thantos could not understand what made these extremely hard rocks so valuable.

Menno District declared war upon the Descendants of Gaea without hesitation, all for these hard rocks, but Carl and his companions threw them away as though they were garbage. He'd sent the shiny rocks to Vitos as a gift. When Vitos opened the gift his mouth began to twitch. And now what surprised him the most is that these creatures who call themselves human are willing to exchange the rocks for Aerolite treasure. Thantos told them, in all honesty, that the stones were useless and could never compare to the Aerolite treasures, but the humans didn't listen. They sent out most of their fleet in search of Aerolite treasures from the four corners of the universe in order to trade it for those hard rocks! Thantos and his people believed that maybe the humans had rocks for brains. What possible use could they have for them?

But then Thantos figured that different civilizations would have differing values. He still remembered Aethos, the representative of Menno District, was too happy to contain himself and almost smashed the table when he announced the minor trade agreement for the stones. He was astounded that the humans treated the useless hard rocks as precious stones. He understood that the stones held some special value to the humans, just as he and his people utilized Stardust and Aerolite Core to extend life; to humans, exposure to the Aerolite core is lethal after extended exposure.

As to why he was willing to join the Empire fleet,, Thantos argued with the force of justice that he was willing to use Gaea's body to cover the gap of values, because it is clearly the humans' loss exchanging Aerolite treasure for worthless stones. But erudite Aquos mercilessly exposed him. This is because Thantos coveted Aerolites that hadn't been exploited in the Galaxy.

It seems that the big guy is not so simple and honest as people imagine. But the Empire fleet did not expose his lie, because they knew it was far more valuable to have his strong help than all those useless Aerolites.
story.STORY_FLEET_160:
The Empire insisted that the government's top-secret files would be opened to the public after 100 years. This not only relates to the security of a secret character and the Empire, but also maintains the public's right to know. The people excercise this right in many ways. One hobby is to study the legendaries' early experiences and victories during war time.

Razz, a scrapper since birth, was born in the slums of Rocky Star, and learned at an early age to fight for what he wanted. To make a living, he joined up with the mercenary industry. There was a high risk, very high mortality rate, but he took to it as though born with a weapon in each hand. He overcame all obstacles and became a good mercenary, while many boys who'd entered at the same time died during training excercises. But those who rose together bonded with their newfound brothers, and would give their lives for one another without hesitation. Razz grew fond of his team members. Too bad he would outlive them all...

One last mission: His employer charged he and his crew with the assassination of an affairs office member named Sokolov. What the crew didn't know was that there was a pair of Empire Corp units with standard configuration and protection technologies that had never been published by the Ministry of Science and Technology. Sokolov was definitely not "just" another hit. 

The last of his crew evaporated in a hail of particle blasts as he tried to draw their fire, giving Razz an opportunity to get at Sokolov. Wounded and bleeding, Razz tried to focus and aim straight, but loss of blood had made him dizzy. The shot meant for Sokolov struck a painting  behind the man, and Razz lost consciousness.

Suprised to be alive, Razz awakens in a hospital bed. He'd been spared by Sokolov because of the man's appreciation for soldiers who sacrifice everything to complete their task. Sokolov used his influence to expunge all records of Razz and his mercenary background, and recommended him to join the Empire Fleet.

Although he'd lost all of his teammates and his life as a mercenary, Razz reluctantly accepted his new identity. He would carry on - if not for himself, then for those brothers he'd left behind. Their memory would live on through him as long as he drew breath.

"Behind all heroes, it seems there is a poignant story."

"However, because of the presence of heroes, the Empire stands one step closer on the path to victory."
story.STORY_FLEET_157:
No one really knows the true reason behind the aggressive missions to expand territory of the Human race. Is it because of "overpopulation" and "depleting resources" as they repeatedly state over and over in the federal propaganda films, or simply as some of the top fleet commanders suggest: that "going to war is the only way to ensure the survival of human race in the vast and cruel Galaxy"? 

Carter used to believe that "war" was nothing but the result of politicians' ambition. But now, even for someone like Carter, there is no room for indifference...especially now that the human race faces a horde of violent and ruthless alien bug.

The thought of enjoying a good book - old-school paperback or hyper-hologram under the warm library lightning is enough to bring peace to anyone's mind... Although it may very well be just a fantasy for Carter. At this moment, Carter is commanding his fleet in the toughest battle yet, against an alien bug fleet more powerful than anything he has ever faced. No matter whether this war began with the right cause, Carter only has one mission for himself: as long as he is standing on the bridge of his flagship, no human will fall to the bugs. Not on his watch. 

Another victory! Carter's assistant sent word of their victory to the Allied Fleets. Congradulatory Messages poured in as cheers rang through the ship. But, win or lose, Carter opted to not reply; victory and defeat is relative in the end. No one can win them all. One day he would lose. "What will those voices chattering over the comms say then? He must stand resolute. A good commander cannot allow victory to paralyze him."

Carter retreated to his cabin and lay down to collect his thoughts. In his mind, the universe seemed endless. How many races existed? How many would be enemies of the human race - how many would be friends to mankind? Even as these images raced through his mind, he knew there were no answers forthcoming: imagining blueprints that cannot be realized is like thinking of a lullaby. In thinking of it, sleep never comes. Carter didn't know all, but he could see that the war grew more desperate as the days passed. Since sleep was not going to happen, he decided to get a cup of tea and read another book.

For humans, nothing can be absolute. Also, it didn't hurt to learn something new.
story.STORY_FLEET_181:
What a peaceful world! However, when the work insects throw the mixture of food and digestive juices into the nest, everything becomes chaotic. The larvae start to attack their sisters and brothers to snatch the limited resources for survival using their bodies and their newborn energy weapons. Quasimodo is the exception. He stares at them with his compound eyes and fear gradually fills their hearts. They find out that that which stands before them is a creepy creature and is in fact not a delicious from of sustenance, and the shock causes them to rapidly flee. Quasimodo then slowly lurches forwards and starts to tuck into his breakfast.
Quasimodo had a vague feeling that he was different from others even before he was spewed out into this world. Within a certain range he can observe what happens around him with the use of oocysts tuned by his mental acuity. This oocyst is like a sensory organ which is more subtle than the compound eyes of flies; essentially a 360 degree holographic projection with no blind spots with which he can veen read others' minds. With the gradually growing power of this sensory organ, his spiritual power was extended to the entire population on the day he left the nest. However, observing this world earlier than others didn’t fill Quasimodo with pleasant memories, it simply made him question himself: even though he was born, educated, and battle-trained as a bug larvae, he in fact may not really be a bug.
Therefore the question then became who is Quasimodo and where does he belong? Quasimodo and his cousins finally grew up and they had to face the first race to determine their fate. Were they going to be soldiers plundering resources from other planets, or low-level workers there to feed larvae? In his heart of hearts, young Quasimodo certainly hoped to become the most powerful warrior to have ever battled amongst the planets and he became the ultimate winner through his spiritual power and unique illusory powers, but he also became the first exiled winner in the Bugs' history, because the Queen’s Pro guard discovered his ability and determined him to be a potential, uncontrollable threat.
Quasimodo since became an interstellar vagrant since he could not be a member of the bugs and fight for them. If your destiny is undefined, you can go anywhere you want to go, right?
story.STORY_FLEET_186:
Striker harkened back to Leaves, the planet he once called home; a planet which now stands in ruins, destroyed by enemy missiles. Nothing was left alive, and his once ripe and lush orchard was gone ... The dream was always the same. There is one thing he could have done to prevent the destuction, but Striker was paralyzed, unable to lift a finger... In this dream...

Striker, following orders from the supreme commander, fought a battle and devastated the enemy forces. They were crippled and would have been easy prey, but he allowed them to escape. The battered and beaten enemy was so bent upon the destruction of Leaves planet that they left their home base defenses without support. Fleet command sacrificed Leaves in order to anhilate the enemy home base, which eventually led to total victory.

Aside from the defense fortress on Leaves in the Hima Star system, its residents are farmers. They harvested the Leaves Fruits. Though they will be sorely missed, one planet in a star system is like a leaf on a giant tree. One withered leaf would not kill the entire tree.

Striker and his troops - fine warriors all - received medals of the highest honor, but the medals couldn't bring back all that they had lost. All they had ever known and loved was now dust.

Striker threw his medal into a black hole and turned his back on his commision. He joined with the space mercenaries. They were purposeless, cared for nothing, and worked for bounties - the higher the better, and the more dangerous task even better! The aggresive strategies they plied would never be something the Fleet would dare use. Striker slipped away into his new persona, his new life of debauchery, filling himself with the finest wine, and spending bounty money on women. 

Never again would he show mercy to an enemy. He would destroy them completely, or they would kill him. There would be no grey area ... Battleship after battleship, he would kill for the thrill, the excitement, the death. But no matter how many foes he vanquished, their dying screams filling his ears, he could still hear Leaves. Its echo filled his mind and rebounded through his dreams.

One by one, his comrades left him; some lost to war, and others lost to women they decided to marry and settle down on another planet. Striker found himself alone in the end, alone with his memories and hunger for a retribution that could never be sated. In the end he chose to settle down in the Empire Fleet.

Striker never blamed the commander who ordered him to let the enemy escape to destroy his home planet of Leaves. He was a soldier, and he understood that schemes and sacrifices must be made for the greater good. Victory often came with great loss when dealing with a greater adversary. But now Striker has found all the power he needs.

His only hope is that he will one day be able to put the past to rest, and silence the rustling ghost that haunts his dreams... the sound of Leaves.
story.STORY_FLEET_187:
Warden was quite the entrepeneur...

Lyon wanted to catch a movie with Sylver after dinner. Warden appreciated puppy love, but he also liked money. That's why he took a few credits from Lyon as compensation for covering his shift. "If ya wanna play, ya gotta pay". That was a motto Warden loved to quote. Lyon was his comrade and all, but money was money. Warden wasn't really a "nice guy".

He deals with those who ask him for help using this motto: "If you don't pay, how could you appreciate the value of the goods, or the time". Favors were nice, but Warden never, ever did anything for free. As long as there were cubits or credits to be had, Warden would do all he could to complete whatever arrangement he'd made with a "friend". He certainly was a successful businessman. Some might even say he was a decent comrade, but he was never named a good friend.

He wasn't a Scrooge. Warden had several factories in some of the largest star systems. These factories were built next to major rehabilitation centers, and employed both physical and mentally handicapped patients. In all honesty, most of the products produced were hardly good enough to put out in the shops, but Warden always made sure those workers received their paychecks on time.

You will not realize your value without contribution.

Ten years ago, Warden had a beautiful girlfriend. She was a nurse and loved to lend a hand where she could. The nurse's involvement with charity actually became her burden, because you know ... not everyone is a billionaire.

She and Warden embarked upon a deep space adventure to hopefully find an erupting white hole, so that they could harvest galaconite energy and resolve their financial concerns for good. However, a few years later only Warden's sleeping capsule was found by a rescue team. His beautiful girlfriend had perished in deep space.

After his rescue, Warden returned to the Empire Fleet and kept on fighting. But he became the infamous "Scrooge of the Empire Fleet": You get what you pay for. Such actions didn't actually fall in line with Empire code of conduct, but he managed to walk the fine line and stay within the legal limits.

Perhaps the Empire pays Warden handsomely. Why else would he never try to bargain with the Empire Fleet's orders? Each of his hard-won battles was perfect.
story.STORY_FLEET_173:
Possibly because this star district is the closest to the Abyss, but Incendos and his mates of the Sara Mande District are able to utilize the power of energy across all of the Elemental Dimension.

Energy is the source of life - no matter to Vitos, who can remain motionless for years at a time; or to Thantos, who sees stardust radiation as something more important than his own well being. The warriors of the Sara Mande District spend most of their time battling in the Menno Chaos District and the the Abyss, their knowledge and skills hard earned during every moment of life-and-death battles. 

Without question, Incendos is among their finest. The armies of the Abyss have a nearly flawless system which enables them to absorb and reflect energy attacks. The formidable fleets must see them as a bottomless black hole; no matter how powerful the energy attack is, Incendos's troops can always absorb and counter with an attack that is a few times stronger than their foe's. There are countless unique fleets in the Elemental Dimension, but only Incendos's fleet has a time-tested method to reduce the effectiveness of the counter-attack strategy of the Abyss. Every kind of attack relates to the way you utilize energy. As long as you understand energy, the "unbeatable" fleet of the Abyss is no longer an "unbeatable legend".

But that's not enough for Incendos. The fire burning in his gut has turned from amber to bright-white: this is the beginning of his wrath! The "God of Destroyers" is calling for a new battle, a new search for inspiration that can only find fruition during the test of life and death.

Hey you, are you my new opponent?
story.STORY_FLEET_215:
He ate his last hamburger dinner, signed the agreement of compensation, wrote a will, and had a last one-way dialogue with his wife. With no regrets, he could now die a hero.

The landing pod carries barely enough fuel for the landing. Humans know little of the mechanics of the Bugs, and this pod was designed for unmanned explorations of dangerous planets, but it is now rented to the army for them to carry out dangerous missions. Murphy presses his brow against the rough multi-tube laser cannons and closes his eyes. He needs the cold barrel to cool him down and stop the tears from falling. Soon the laser cannons will be red hot as they pour destruction down upon the battlefield. His only hope is to complete the mission before the cannons become so hot that they explode. When that happens he will become dinner for the Bugs, but he's alright with that. 

The mission for Murphy's team was to land in the area occupied by the Bugs and blow up the nest. Fifteen men prepared to lay down their lives for this mission...for thier compensation. Before the mission's launch, the scientific research institute had sent its people to evaluate and give every man "psychological counceling", and "encouraging chips" were implanted into each man's skull. The chip, as it turned out, proved to be useless. 

Murphy pulled his face away from the cannon's cold steel, took a nervous breath as the pod shuddered violently upon entering the planet's atmosphere. He studied the mini-nuclear bombs. Soon, they could come in handy.

...............

When next Murphy opens his eyes, 200 years have passed. He found himself at the imperial royal medical rehabilitation center. As it turns out, the "encouraging chip" was actually a consciousness collector developed by the scientists of the academy. It should take many years, and precious resources to train a soldier. The scientists were secretly researching a way to capture a soldier's soul at the moment of death, and keep it. The experiment was shut down not long after it began due to some serious flaws, but not before the first batch of test subjects were used. Murphy and his boys were those subjects. They were the first and last. As far as Murphy knows he was the only soldier whose chip remained intact, but even still there were defects. His memory remains incomplete due to "unknown factors". According to official military ducuments, thier mission to blow the bug nest was a complete success, but he can't remember anything after exiting the pod. Probably for the best; who wants to recall their own death? Most soldiers spent months, or even years of seeing a shrink recovering from a near-death experience. 

Murphy took up the latest laser gun given to him by the Empire. There was no need to worry about it overheating in his hand, or exploding from overuse. Since his "resurrection" a clear line had been established between the Empire and the Bugs, so there was no need for precautions against the bugs either. Today, Murphy's new life - his rebirth - as an interstellar cop, has begun.
story.STORY_FLEET_179:
Last night, an explosion rocked the residence of Daleks, the eldest son of Sivori. Daleks was the new prosecutor assigned to the bribery case of ex-senator Sivori. When police examined the scene of the explosion, no body was discovered. The Truth News reported that the suspect of the explosion was Sivori's political enemy who had framed Sivori in the first place, and wanted the eldest son dead after learning that young Sivori had been given the evidence of his father's innocence...

"Hey, are you the fellow on the Truth News?" The rebel in a red uniform says to the body lying in the repair capsule. "Senator Sivori suggested implementing an upper cap for the Empire's tax and labor duty on the colonies. Of course, those Empire morons would never let that happen. All you can do now is lay there. Geez, lost half your face, an arm and a leg...but at least you're still alive, right?"

In the blink of an eye, Daleks has spent several years in the rebel fleet, and has even participated in many battles against the Empire. His hatred for the Empire burns as strongly as his former love of the Empire. Daleks refused to rebuild his body through operations. Instead, he ordered a lighter, stronger exterior robotic armor and bone structure. Because the crucial evidence had been destroyed in the fire, and Daleks was gone, Sivori had been exiled to a barren star. Each time Daleks gazes down the length of his handicapped body he is reminded of the explosion that maimed him, and the Empire's prosecution.

During the battle of Alan Star district colony, Daleks met an old friend of Sivori, a rebel general named Max. He was a kind, bearded middle aged man who loved his drink. Max invited Daleks to stay in Alan Star district after the battles. Although the rebel army consisted of many people who have fled to the Alan Star system due to the Empire's suppression, it was also rife with thugs and criminals. 

Unfortunately, the second year after Daleks joined the colony rebel forces, Max was seriously injured in an accident. He'd been betrayed by his subordinate. Before he died, he gave Daleks one last assignment: The Empire is still trustworthy, but the worms continue to rot away the beautiful nation. The evidence Daleks had found years before was already starting to affect the "benefit chains" of Empire worms. Fighting against the Empire is not the right way to get revenge. The right thing to do is to find those responsible for framing his father and bring them to justice.

No one knows what happened after this. The Empire prosecuted the "bribery chain", led by the Secretary of Treasury and Speaker of the House. Some say it was because a group of commanders filed a report against them at the Empire HQ. Others say that at last Daleks, the eldest son of Sivori who have been persecuted all those years ago has regained the evidence to put down the political bribery tycoon. 

In the faraway Alan star district, Daleks purchases the most recent copy of "Empire Colony Policy" from a galaxy merchant, and then vanishes into the darkness.
story.STORY_FLEET_180:
In the times of Ancient Earth, there was a philologist who proposed a dialectical analysis on the principle of the human race: Is a Human born good, or evil?

Our intelligence, ability to feel, rationalize, adapt to sudden changes in our environments have allowed humankind to flourish and become the species that rules all others, and created a civilization that stretched across the galaxy. However, the human race is also responsible for the extinction of countless species, as well as the destruction of many planets environments, and depleting colony resources...

Are we the creator of all known civilizations in the galaxy, or are we the destroyers born with a sin from Planet Earth?

Goodman believes that we all are born in the most primitive form; kind, loving and pure; we are angels, sent by God to spread love and peace to all corners of the known galaxy. For decades he held to his beliefs: even though we have never found physical evidence of God's existence, we need to find the sanctuary within our own hearts.

Given his belief structure, Goodman held faith. The Empire has been implimenting its aggressive diplomatic methods to expand territory; to colonize planets; to clone commanders and armies to conquer other civilizations. Treason, betrayal, scheming - all of these acts surrounded Goodman as he remained true to his beliefs. His battle career took a toll on him in more ways than merely physical...

"We are better than this..." Goodman mumbled to himself while watching the explosions of his colleague's ships. Since the discovery of the Elemental Dimension, the human fleets have poured into the district under the banner of "peace" (or at least they say for peace). Goodman didn't join any of the Fleet expiditions. Instead, disenchanted by the treacherous nature of his brethren, he and his squadron left the Empire Fleet and, some say, disappeared into the Elemental Dimension. 

Just when people were about to place his name in the Hall of Fame Memorial Cemetery, Goodman reappeared in the Hellgate, more powerful than ever and with an unbreakable belief. 

Goodman's ship, baptized by the flame of Hellgate, has returned. 

"I never gave up on the notion that we are all born with kindness in our hearts," he said, then his brow furrowed as he clenched his fists. "But I am starting to believe that the kindhearted should not allow innocents to suffer tyranny."
story.STORY_FLEET_184:
In ancient times, The Overseer Lighthouse Tower was known as the crucial "Tower of Life" - a lone sentinel on the border of the Empire, but now it is nothing more than an isolated castle.

With each step forward for technology and civilization, it is inevitable that something of the past gets left behind. Mileena's family line acted as Overseer of what was known as "The Land of Devils", located at the Empire's borderline. Their responsibilities were to observe any changes in the black hole's gravity field, and to send out travel warnings to stay away from the area. The enormous black hole, which spanned three star districts, has caused the entire district to be named "The No-Life-Zone" because of its unstable gravity field. Over the years, the once grand tower of life has become nothing more than Mileena's family prison.

A few hundred years before warping technology matured to its present state, the Overseers post was a most revered and respected duty. Their sacrifice of time, freedom - and sometimes their lives - in exchange for the safety of travellers and valuable data collection was applauded by all. Poets and songmasters sang their praises. Now, their title, their sacrifice, and names is long forgotten and may only be found if one were to search through the dusty tomes of yesteryear...

Ever since the last of her cousins died, only Mileena remained in the Lighthouse Tower. Cloning had become the only way to carry on the family line. Even Mileena was a clone of the original Mileena. Born in an artificial womb, she calls her maker "sister". All her life, Mileena had prepared to spend the remainder of her years as an Overseer. She saw this as her duty. But a sudden tremor in the black hole space pushed the readings to a never-before seen climax, then all activity stopped, including the gravity field...

Which had dissapeared entirely!

Mileena hurriedly jumped into her spaceship, "Tana", to enter the field to inspect the instruments for possible errors, but all she was met with were beautiful, bright stars. Light rays from the star systems were no longer swallowed by the black hole, but reflected into wondrous spectrum by other planets.

"Freedom!"

of a sort...

"This is my rebirth," Mileena whispered to Tana on the first day reporting at the Empire Fleet.
story.STORY_FLEET_162:
The princess of the Empire was attacked and kidnapped by the Imperial Army as she rushed back to her father's funeral. She spent years imprisoned in an alien base. Several years later, after a huge battle, she returned to the empire to seek her vengeance upon the schemer who'd attacked her people. Once there she discovered that her attacker had failed all those years ago while attempting wrest power, and had been slain. 

What could be more disappointing than having a well-planned punch fall short of its mark? Zooey remained with the fleet to continue service to the Empire. She had an easy childhood, and her teen years stayed uneventful. She didn't strive for the throne, but was attacked during her journey home before graduation to attend her father's funeral, and wrongly assumed missing. After her capture, many hardships fell upon her, but she rose to meet the challenges, and after some time was able to attain enough power to return home and strike down her enemies. All in vain, though, because the enemy's grave was old enough to be covered by many long vines. 

Disappointed but not ready to quit, Zooey put on smoked makeup and painted her beloved fleet with phantom purple. There was nothing she could do about the dead enemies, but there was something she could do about those involved who still drew breath: she would hunt them down and take out her vengeance upon them. 

Zooey is a princess of the Empire, but she is also the most outstanding student of the military academy. Thanks to the name on the grave stone, she tasted a side of life she may never had otherwise. The hymn of the darkness should be sent to all those conspirators involved in the attack. She would collect their very souls herself. All would pay...
story.STORY_FLEET_191:
The Data of Life: Utilize information to convert a lifetime of experiences and memory into data, then upload into cloud storage. Using the Empire's top-secret laboratory technical support and a reserved body to back up the data, the "code of life" has been breached.

But this technology has been in existence for over 200 years. The once "Darrien-the-Great" has become an old man, and needs to submerge himself in "revitalizing fluid" for 12 hours each day. The fluid is capable of repairing damaged and worn out body parts, but is slowly but surely falling behind with Darrien's failing organs, and his time between submersion in the liquid becomes shorter each passing day. 

Darrien gazes jealously at the young technicians as they drag away the fluid tubes. His eyes fall to his own health inspection report. Bad news, it says. If he doesn't finish his research soon, he will die. He shook his head as he crumpled the report and tossed it away. He has decided to challenge the fine line between science and morality... 

Thus the "Data of Life" project has begun. Under Darrien's leadership, the experiment has entered its final testing stage. Deemed "unethical" by the general population, the government has secretly provided funding and donated experimental bodies for the project. Their motives are transparent: the success of the project means extending the lives of aging high-ranking officials and royalty. Also, if the expense is low enough, they could even slash much of the budget of the Empire Military School, because every soldier will become a "war machine". Even if the soldier's body suffers unrepairable damage, as long as the chip is intact, their life will simply be installed into a new body, and they can continue serving the Empire.

But the first phase didn't provide ideal feedback. Of the 15 experimental bodies that were implanted with the chips, an EEG pulse could be recovered from only one: Code name F_07, Empire 30th army corp, 2nd class private, Murphy. 

The success rate is a mere 7%, and Murphy displayed a certain degree of memory loss and elevated agression. The procedures conducted in the first phase had been flawless, with 100% normal readings. But Darrien knew...

It was a warning from God. 

And so the agressive #7 was locked away in a cryo capsule. 

The first phase experience was widely opposed by the public before its announcement was even finished. The Empire has given up on the "Data of Life" project, but Darrien has not. He couldn't. His very life hangs in the balance.

Can Darrien eventually break the "Rules" of a game created by God himself?

For the sake of his own survival, he will try...
story.STORY_FLEET_193:
DETACH ROBOTIC ARM...DW38XE-SERIES PARTS SEVERELY DAMAGED...REPLACED.

INSPECT POWER TRACK BELTS...THREE LOOSE SCREWS...TIGHTENED.

OPEN CHEST COMPARTMENT...

Within the steel walls of the chest cavity, slightly to the left of the neon blue air purification system, a dark red heart beats slowly and assertively. His heart and brain are all that remain of his original self. Countless operations and upgrades have left him more machine than man, and the last remaining vestiges to prove he was ever human at all.

The organs of thought and feeling may remain, but he senses that his feelings are waning. Boris can recall the rainy day when he broke up with his first girlfriend; the moment he ran into the rain and tossed his umbrella to the ground; but could not remember the reason, the feelings he felt at that moment. He can remember the Thanksgiving feast he attended with his parents as a child; can see the wrinkles on his father's face and the white of his mother's hair; but he can't recall the warmth of being surrounded by loved ones. Of course, Boris could recount with great detail the events surrounding the loss of his right arm and upper right torso during a skirmish with Alien Bugs, and that he chose to be modified by robotics rather than to retire.

...What kind of emotion is loyalty? Is it worth the loss of life and the ability to laugh, to love, to feel anything at all?

The doubt was short lived. Full body diagnostic was soon over. The robotic body requires maintenance only once every three years. He is sound again. Ready. Unlike a human, whose fragile bodies would not withstand a slight laser blast or high level radiation, he would persevere.

CLOSE CHEST COMPARTMENT...AIR PURIFICATION SYSTEM CLEANING COMPLETE.

POWER TRACK BELTS OPERATING WITHIN SPECIFIED PARAMETERS. ABLE TO ACCELERATE FROM 0-300KM IN 0.1 SECONDS.

REINSTALLED ROBOTIC ARM. DEXTERITY...CHECK. OPERATION RESTORED. FOLLOWING FULL COMMAND FROM THE BRAIN.

Boris doesn't care anymore whether he is "alive" or not. He lives for the mission. Orders, battles and victories are his reason to "be".
story.STORY_FLEET_161:
The storm that rages across the planet surface, the constantly burning element, the black hole that swallows them all ... Nature is both the cradle of life, and the resting place of all.

When Khala asked Vela'rath the reason for leaving Nami planet, Vela'rath didn't give the real reason. To doubt ones belief is far more difficult than to build it. And what about after doubting ones belief? How would the residents of Nami planet regain their belief, when they see Mother Nature as their source of power?

While searching through ruins in the human star system, Vela'rath happened upon an engraved stone. The letters were so worn as to almost be gone, but not quite. They read: "When you are told that mountains are mountains, and water is water...what if mountains are not mountains, and water is not water? After all, mountains are still mountains, and water is always water." 

No matter how the ancient humans interpreted this phrase, this has set the foundation for Vela'rath to alter his own beliefs. After his discovery, he has ventured through every ancient human settlement or ruins to learn all he could. No exact reason or purpose ... he just wanted to learn all he could.

Meeting the human at Kilimanjar is no coincidence. Vela'rath had made up his mind to meet someone - anyone - from the human race after his long trek through their past, their ruins. But ruins represent the past, and he wanted to know about the human race as is now. How have they developed through the Galaxy Empire era? What new philosophy could they impart now?

Vela'rath looks forward to studying the human, and as many other intelligent life forms as he can find, in order to find structure for his own beliefs.
story.STORY_FLEET_194:
To survive is to be victorious.

This has been a rule of the battlefield since ancient times. But now, the interstellar battlefield, "scavenger" team members are accostomed to finding repairable - perhaps even intact - battleships, but rarely are there wounded found remaining in the battlefield after the fleet retreats. 

When the Battle of Felix, between humans and Shadow Will (also known as the "chaotic reality") ended a week ago, the Empire fleet scavengers found an unharmed but severely dehydrated and unconscious man in an abandoned stronghold of Shadow Will: the White Star which had become a pile of scrap iron. Judging by his clothes, he may be a general of the Divine Alliance, but the man's DNA is not found in the gene pool of the Divine Alliance.

He may have strayed innocently into the battlefield, his navigation system may have malfunctioned, but he may also be an enemy, prisoner of war, or even a spy...

The Battle of Felix suffered severe losses, and to give special treatment to the unharmed man found inside the White Star is ridiculous. Many family members of fallen soldiers organized a protest when they learned of the man's special treatment. They claimed that the man in the coma should be transferred to the military prison from the Royal Hospital, under the charge of espionage.

To the Empire, the demands of the people seem simple and direct. Many lost loved ones in the battle and needed an outlet for their grief. Humankind had seen the power of the Shadow Will, and the Empire had prepared for war. They treated the soldiers and the families of the dead well. After winning the battle a suspect appears - it's not a big deal, but can become the fuse of public sentiment.

Hartmann awoke in a waiting hall of a military court, and from there was sent to the Oswy stars in a nutrition rehabilitation pod.

The losers are villified as bandits, failed in a faction war of the Divine Alliance. Hartmann had prepared for death, but is not prepared to be called a "human traitor", to lose all honor and rot in the grave of a sinner.

So, to survive is to be victorious. Regardless of how long it took, he vowed to one day return to the galaxy.
story.STORY_FLEET_192:
Katiya swore that he'd received the order to retreat, but the classified military orders had disappeared without a trace. The consequences being dozens of star sections slaughtered wholesale by the rebels, and no resistance was offered.

And so he decided to leave the Galaxy Empire. There was nothing left to hold him anymore. His parents had died in the early Bug attacks, and he had few people he'd miss - possibly a comrade or two. He stockpiles energy, cross-checks the star map, and looks forward to traveling to a new place to make a fresh start.

Katiya's great grandfather was the commander of Barnard Empire, but later became the Galaxy Empire's "guest". Happenings from 400 years ago are not worth remembering, and that's likely why Katiya sunk to obscurity in the Empire Fleet, in spite of his bravery on the battlefield, and might possibly be the reason he suffered exclusion and was framed.

He set the coordinates for the Andromeda galaxy, to the city of Stormrage. He found out about this place during an information exchange seminar. The city of Stormrage was founded by the Barnard people who refused to surrender to the Empire 400 years ago. Galaxy Empire, although aware of its existence, has no intention of wiping them out, but instead adopted the attitude that Stormrage couldn't ever be a threat to the Empire. After so long, and the fact that the Andromeda galaxy was not a human settlement, why would they bother with them?

When Katiya's ship was two million light years from the Galaxy, a confidential report from the Fourth Fleet was placed below the Emperor's tea cup. It detailed a report of an admiral who suppressed talents, and let his nephew take credit for their work. The man had even framed collegues. The Emperor immediately ordered the admiral arrested, but the commanders who had leave of the Galaxy had already blocked all forms of communication from the Empire.

Temporarily forget the past, because tomorrow is a new beginning.
story.STORY_FLEET_188:
She removes the steaming oatmeal bread from the oven, brews a cup of hand-ground coffee. In fact, Phoebe prefers to use nutrition to supply a whole day's worth of consumption, rather than spending credits to enjoy ancient and traditional food.
        When did this bizarre habit start?
        The piano music is light and melodious, Phoebe's favourite electric guitar album is covered with thick dust on the table, since Taylor's death, Phoebe hasn't opened them once.
        Death took Taylor's breath away, it also numbed Phoebe's emotions, she wants to forget it, but it may take another 200 years. Unconsciously, Taylor's thoughts, Taylor's habits have been etched deeply into Phoebe's soul. Compared with Phoebe's long life, even when medical technology has significantly extended the human life span, the time Taylor spent alive is still just a fleeting moment.
        200 years of happiness and joy, Phoebe will suffer even more pain to spend the following years without Taylor near her.
        Racial differences created an irony, back when Phoebe and Taylor decided to enter into marriage, humans had established diplomatic relations with the Morn planet, who have a genetic difference of around 5%. Morn males are twice as strong as human males, but their women are more similarly matched to human women, just taller and more beautiful. Beauty is the eternal pursuit, but facing a beauty whose life span may be 3 times more than yours, perhaps breeds more fear than joy.
        If only time could be stalled forever, everything would be fine. It is such a pity that Taylor became just a fragment of Phoebe's life.
story.STORY_FLEET_190:
Krill sits upon the stairs leading up to the Pandemonium and inspects the spoils of war from his most recent battle with the human fleets. It's a miniature projector displaying a human girl's image when the cover is opened. 

Sadness, regret, agony...death? He gazes at the little face. What do you hope to be saved from, little human?

An unfamiliar mood descended upon Krill. He tried to recall the facial expression of the original human owner of the projector just before he was killed; it was very different from the "desperation" Krill had seen in the past. 

Perhaps this new mood he's discovered is called "jealousy".
